control: C1 the projection is kept out of the flush path
why: I08. If apply_projection/2 marked the key dirty, a recorded event would also be flushed into aurora_meter_counters, which is the table Pro bills from.

control: C2 a conflicting payload is not accepted as a duplicate
why: I07, and the single largest residual risk this unit names: an implementer 'simplifying' the hash comparison away turns a conflicting reuse of an identity into a silent duplicate, which is how a retry bills twice.

control: C3 a duplicate adds no second totals delta
why: I06. Applying the totals delta to every returned row rather than to the inserted ones makes a retry after an uncertain write count twice.

control: C4 a refused durable write never becomes a buffered one
why: L-03b-4. A fallback to track/4 on overload would leave the caller believing a fact was recorded that has no identity and no way to be deduplicated.

control: C5 the request-size bound measures what the caller sent
why: X104. Measuring anything other than the bytes on the wire lets a compressible payload of any size through, which is what pg_column_size() did.
